From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: julie.sullivan@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action Required: Targeted Region Peering Degradation — Endpoint Preference Instructions

Hi Julie / FinTech ops team,

We observed a targeted peering degradation affecting egress from our eu-central and apac-southeast clusters beginning ~08:50 UTC this morning. Symptoms we saw: higher tail latency for token-generation requests and an increase in 502/503 responses for requests routed through those regions. Our control plane enacted automated fallback routing to adjacent regions (primarily us-west and eu-west), but that resulted in increased cross-region egress and higher p99 latency for some customers.

What we recommend now (short window, low-risk):
- If you can accept the traffic being served from a single non-local region for the next 24–48h, do nothing — our fallback keeps serving.
- If you prefer to avoid cross-region egress and are OK routing to the region with the best current health, switch to the regional endpoint for your preferred region. Example: set endpoint to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/region-eu-west/generate or set the prefer_local_region flag to false and region_preference to "eu-west".

Quick CURL example to pin to eu-west:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/region-eu-west/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":256}'

We've attached a one-page snippet (customer_reroute_snippet.sh) with exact CLI/SDK examples for common languages and a short checklist. Also linking the public incident page: https://redwood.statuspage.io/incidents/4782.

We will continue monitoring and will share a short post-incident summary once root cause and remediation are complete. If you want Redwood to perform a temporary routing override for your account (we can do that from our side), reply with the account id and the target region and we'll apply it within 30 minutes.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Julie,

Quick answers and actions we've taken:
- Root cause & ETA: Our infra team is investigating a peering flap on the provider side; initial ETA from their network team is 8–18 hours for stabilization, but that's tentative.
- In-flight requests: switching the endpoint (or setting a regional endpoint) is a client-side config change. In-flight requests to the previous endpoint will complete or fail based on that request's lifecycle — there is no data loss. We recommend performing the change during a low-traffic window if you have long-running sessions.
- Temporary override: we can set a routing override for FinTechCo to prefer eu-west (or us-west, whichever you name) for up to 48 hours. If you'd like us to do it, reply with the account id (or allow me to use FTCO-2213).

Attached is a short checklist and the exact SDK example we suggest. If you prefer we do the override, we'll apply it and confirm.

Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — Incident INC-4782 (peering degradation)

Hi Julie and FinTechCo team,

Thank you again for the quick coordination. This is the short post-incident update and actions taken on our side:

Summary:
- Window: 2028-10-30 08:50 UTC to 2028-10-31 02:15 UTC (degradation observed).
- Impact: Increased p99 latency and elevated 502/503 errors for requests routed through eu-central and apac-southeast. Some customer traffic was temporarily routed to neighboring regions, which increased egress latency for a subset of requests.
- Action taken: Per your approval (Julie), we applied a temporary routing override for FTCO-2213 to prefer eu-west starting 2028-10-30 11:12 UTC. We validated reduced cross-region egress and saw client-side success rate improve to baseline within ~18 minutes.

Root cause (high level): Intermittent peering flap between our provider and a regional exchange; provider has applied a mitigation and is performing post-change validation. We are pursuing a long-term mitigation with them to avoid recurrence.

Customer-facing guidance (for your ops runbook):
1) If you see similar latency or 5xxs and want to avoid cross-region egress, you can switch to a regional endpoint (examples in the attached appendix).
2) We can perform temporary per-account routing overrides on request — contact your account rep or reply to this thread with the account id and target region.
3) After provider confirms stabilization, we will remove routing overrides and notify you 24h in advance.

Attachments: redwood_incident_appendix.pdf (contains SDK snippets, checklist, and validation commands).

Open items for Redwood:
- Follow up with provider for a permanent peering remediation (Owner: Neha)
- Publish full technical postmortem to shared drive and link it on status page (Owner: Sean)
- Send an ops-friendly one-page summary for FinTechCo compliance (Owner: Laura)

If you want the full technical postmortem now, reply and we'll share the draft. We appreciate the partnership — apologies for the disruption, and please reach out if anything else appears.

— Rafael Mendes

Redwood Inference
